title: Kenafric KPI review submission (v1.0)
description: The body of a POST to WF-26b (kenafric-wf26b): a mid-probation or final review of one employee against their agreed KPI set. One instrument, two modes — the mid review is the final review with the scoring block hidden — and `mode` is echoed back from what the context endpoint said, never chosen by the browser. Carries NO scores: Score, Weighted Score, Weighted KPI Score and Final Individual Score are all WF-26b's, and Weighted Score is a ClickUp formula that recomputes itself. Validated against real payloads by src/kpi/payload.test.ts with Ajv.

t.description: The signed token from the link, passed through verbatim. n8n verifies it against LINK_SECRET. It is also what makes a retry harmless: WF-26b appends KMID or KFIN to Automation Markers and refuses a review whose marker is already there.

mode.description: Which review this is, echoed back from the context endpoint so WF-26b branches without decoding its own token twice. 'mid' writes Progress and appends to Mid-Review Notes; 'final' writes Actual, Final Rating and Score, the talent block and both sign-off dates.

submittedAt.description: ISO 8601 with the local UTC offset, never Z. On a final review this timestamp, with the signed token, IS the sign-off — it is written to Employee Sign-off Date and Manager Sign-off Date in place of the KIL sheet's wet-signature boxes (K-4).

kpis.description: One entry per LIVE KPI in the agreed set. A voided KPI is not sent at all — it drops out of the numerator and the denominator both. WF-26b refuses a final review that is missing any live KPI: a partial final review produces a wrong weighted score, and a wrong score is worse than none.

taskId.description: The KPI's ClickUp task id, from the context endpoint. The only ClickUp identifier that crosses the wire, and it has to: matching answers back by KPI name would break the first time a statement was edited.

progress.description: Mid only. The ClickUp Progress option NAME, never its UUID.

midReviewNotes.description: Mid only, and absent when nothing was written. Required by the form at At Risk and Off Track. WF-26b APPENDS it under a dated heading rather than overwriting — the mid note and the final note are both evidence — so an empty string here would append a dated heading with nothing under it.

actual.description: Final, quantitative rows only. What was actually achieved, in the KPI's own unit. WF-26b scores it as min(actual / targetFigure, CAP); K-3 decides the cap, and the app caps at 100% for probation.

rating.description: Final only, and captured for EVERY KPI regardless of measurement type — it is what WF-19 gates on and what HR reads. 1 Did not meet, 2 Partially met, 3 Met, 4 Exceeded, 5 Significantly exceeded. A qualitative KPI is scored from it: rating / 5.

comment.description: Final only, and absent when nothing was written. Required by the form at a rating of 2 or below: a 1 or a 2 is part of what a probation decision rests on, and an unexplained one cannot be put to the employee.

talent.description: The KIL sheet's talent block, rows 20-42. Final reviews only. Absent on a mid review.

capacityBuilding.description: Up to three areas for training, coaching or mentoring. Blank lines are dropped, so an empty array means nothing was written rather than three empty strings. WF-26b joins them with newlines for the ClickUp text field.

careerAspirations.description: Up to two positions the employee is aiming for in the next 1 to 2 years.

employeeComments.description: The employee's own words, as given in the review conversation. Absent when nothing was written.

managerComments.description: Required. This is the paragraph the confirmation conversation is held against.

panelAdjustment.description: Signed, HR only, and absent unless the token says HR and a figure was actually typed. A zero adjustment and no adjustment are the same outcome, but only one of them is a decision somebody made. Added to the weighted score to give Final Individual Score.

allOf.description: A mid review carries progress on every KPI, and no scoring of any kind: a mid review that asks for a score is a final review held early, and managers then anchor the real one to it.
A final review carries a rating on every KPI and the talent block.
